security_audit.summary: The static findings are mostly documentation examples, Semgrep detector patterns, or secure configuration snippets rather than executable malicious code. The main residual concern is that the skill recommends unpinned third-party scanner installation and external scanner execution, which should require user approval and version control.

remediation.suggestion: Pin scanner versions, prefer lockfiles or checksums, and document trusted installation sources before running package managers.
Require explicit user approval before installing tools or scanning repositories, and run scanners with least privilege.
Keep vulnerable snippets clearly labeled and separate from secure examples so users do not reuse them by mistake.

content.user_title: Scan Code With SAST Security Tools
content.value_statement: Security issues can hide in source code before release. This skill guides SAST tool selection, scanning, triage, and remediation across common languages.
actual_capabilities: Selects SAST tools for Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, Ruby, PHP, Go, and Rust projects.
Provides scanner commands for Bandit, Semgrep, ESLint Security, CodeQL, SpotBugs, Brakeman, gosec, and cargo-clippy.
Documents custom Semgrep rules for SQL injection, XSS, hardcoded credentials, path traversal, and command injection.
Gives framework security checks for Django, Flask, Express, Spring Boot, Rails, Laravel, and React.
Includes CI examples for GitHub Actions and GitLab SAST workflows.
Shows a multi-language scanner design for collecting findings and calculating risk scores.
limitations: It needs source code access and compatible local tools to run meaningful scans.
It does not replace runtime testing, penetration testing, or manual exploit validation.
Scanner results require human triage because SAST tools can report false positives.
Package installation and repository scanning may need approval in restricted environments.

use_cases.title: Review a pull request for security defects
use_cases.description: Choose suitable scanners, run targeted checks, and prioritize findings before merge.

use_cases.title: Add SAST checks to CI
use_cases.description: Create repeatable local or CI scan steps with reports that developers can review.

use_cases.title: Create custom secure coding rules
use_cases.description: Draft Semgrep rules for organization-specific patterns and map results to CWE or OWASP categories.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic SAST review
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan this repository for high-risk SAST issues. Identify languages, choose safe local tools, summarize findings, and suggest fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Review framework security settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this web application for framework-specific security issues. Focus on authentication, injection, XSS, secrets, and unsafe configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Design a CI SAST workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CI SAST workflow for this project. Include tool choices, approval points, severity gates, report handling, and triage guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Author custom Semgrep rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Create custom Semgrep rules for these internal security policies. Explain each rule, expected matches, false positive risks, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Scan a Python API for source-level security risks.
output: Bandit and Semgrep are appropriate first-pass tools for this repository.
Highest priority findings include unsafe deserialization, SQL construction, and hardcoded credentials.
Recommended fixes use safe parsers, parameterized queries, and environment-based secret management.

output_examples.input: Add SAST to a pull request workflow.
output: Run targeted scanners on changed files and full scans on protected branches.
Store reports as build artifacts and fail only on reviewed high-severity findings.
Require an approval step before installing new scanner packages in CI.

output_examples.input: Triage scanner findings from a JavaScript service.
output: Group findings by exploitability, affected route, and confidence.
Confirm whether user-controlled data reaches dangerous sinks.
Document accepted false positives with rule names and file locations.

best_practices: Run SAST early in development and repeat it in CI before release.
Use multiple scanners when language coverage and rule quality differ.
Triage by exploitability, confidence, reachable code path, and business impact.
anti_patterns: Blocking every scanner warning without validating exploitability or false positives.
Installing unpinned scanner packages in CI without approval or provenance checks.
Treating SAST as a replacement for runtime testing and secure design review.

faq.question: What does this skill scan?
faq.answer: It guides source code scanning for common vulnerability classes across several languages and frameworks.

faq.question: Does it run tools automatically?
faq.answer: It provides commands and workflows. Users should approve package installation and scanner execution first.

faq.question: Which tools does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Bandit, Semgrep, ESLint Security, SonarQube, CodeQL, PMD, SpotBugs, Brakeman, gosec, and cargo-clippy.

faq.question: Can it write custom rules?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for custom Semgrep rules tied to security policies and vulnerability patterns.

faq.question: Will it find every vulnerability?
faq.answer: No. SAST can miss runtime behavior, configuration drift, business logic issues, and environment-specific weaknesses.

faq.question: How should teams use the results?
faq.answer: Teams should triage findings, confirm data flow, prioritize high-impact issues, and track remediation over time.
